title: Interpreting changes in reported case fatality in endemic zoonoses: an analytical framework and ecological analysis of Lassa fever surveillance in Nigeria, 2017-26
abstract: Background: Nigeria's reported Lassa fever case fatality ratio (CFR) rose from 18.9% at week 23 of 2025 to 25.0% in 2026, prompting concerns over failing clinical care. Because surveillance artefacts can also alter CFRs, candidate mechanisms that published data can resolve were identified and evaluated. This ecological study extracted weekly state-level counts from 474 Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention situation reports (2017-2026). Per a pre-specified plan, years were compared at phase-matched points, year-on-year CFR changes were decomposed into within-state and between-state components, and tipping-point ascertainment shifts calculated. Weekly incident and cumulative published totals were compared post hoc. Of 11 candidate mechanisms, 2 could be evaluated fully and 5 in part. On weekly incident counts, 2026 did not differ from 2025 at the phase-matched midpoint (+0.3 percentage points, 95% CI -5.0 to 7.6); within-state (-1.1, 95% CI -4.7 to 3.0) and between-state (+0.5, -2.0 to 2.9) components spanned zero. Conversely, the published cumulative CFR was 5.4 to 6.2 percentage points higher because 70 deaths were added retrospectively by week 36 outside weekly reports. Reconciling cumulative figures would require 279 missed survivors (6% of suspected cases not confirmed). The 2026 CFR rise came from deaths added to cumulative totals outside the weekly counts, and published data cannot attribute it to care. Endemic zoonotic CFRs cannot serve as clinical outcome measures unless testing volumes, deaths added late, and post-mortem sampling are published alongside case counts. US NSF-NIH-NIFA EEID; UK BBSRC; Birgitta Sintring Fellowship (Uppsala University).

title: Monoclonal antibodies raised against the Junín virus glycoprotein show broad reactivity and provide protection in vivo
abstract: ABSTRACT Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) is a disease caused by the Junín virus (JUNV) that can be fatal in 15%–30% of untreated cases. Although JUNV is the only arenavirus for which efficient therapy and vaccination have been established, its administration is limited. In this study, hybridoma technology was used to generate 30 mouse monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the glycoprotein complex (GPC) of JUNV. Of these 30 mAbs, 26 showed strong cross-binding to GPCs from various arenaviruses. In addition, nine mAbs demonstrated potent neutralizing activity in vitro with a 50% inhibitory concentration of less than 1 μg/mL against a replication-competent chimeric vesicular stomatitis virus expressing JUNV GPC (rVSV-JUNV), as well as the live attenuated JUNV vaccine strain Candid#1. Furthermore, when tested in vivo using a challenge model of rVSV-JUNV in Stat2 −/− mice, five select mAbs significantly reduced viral loads in the spleen when administered prophylactically. Humanized versions of JUNV-1A2, JUNV-1D5, and JUNV-5B12 mAbs, which showed protection in vivo in the Stat2 −/− surrogate model, were produced. These antibodies were evaluated in a guinea pig challenge model of AHF and showed protective efficacy. Escape experiments with these humanized antibodies, as well as previously characterized antibodies, GB03 and JUN1, using rVSV-JUNV resulted in the acquisition of amino acid changes in the GP1 part of the GPC, which directly contacts host receptor transferrin receptor 1, indicating these sites could be key for future therapies. In summary, we generated mAbs that may be valuable for antibody-guided vaccine design and therapeutic development. IMPORTANCE Junín virus (JUNV) is a highly pathogenic virus that causes Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) and is classified as a category A pathogen due to its potential for aerosol transmission and the significant number of annual infections and deaths associated with it. Although effective treatments exist, such as convalescent immune plasma, their availability is limited, and they are ineffective when given after the first week of symptoms. This study is significant because it focuses on developing therapeutic monoclonal antibodies against JUNV with strong in vitro neutralizing activity and protection in both a surrogate mouse model and a guinea pig challenge model of AHF. This has led to promising antibody candidates that could be used as therapeutics to combat ongoing outbreaks.

title_zh: 针对Junín病毒糖蛋白产生的单克隆抗体表现出广泛的反应性,并能在体内提供保护
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) is a disease caused by the Junín virus (JUNV) that can be fatal in 15%–30% of untreated cases. Although JUNV is the only arenavirus for which efficient therapy and vaccination have been established, its administration is limited. In this study, hybridoma technology was used to generate 30 mouse monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the glycoprotein complex (GPC) of JUNV. Of these 30 mAbs, 26 showed strong cross-binding to GPCs from various arenaviruses. In addition, nine mAbs demonstrated potent neutralizing activity in vitro with a 50% inhibitory concentration of less than 1 μg/mL against a replication-competent chimeric vesicular stomatitis virus expressing JUNV GPC (rVSV-JUNV), as well as the live attenuated JUNV vaccine strain Candid#1. Furthermore, when tested in vivo using a challenge model of rVSV-JUNV in Stat2 −/− mice, five select mAbs significantly reduced viral loads in the spleen when administered prophylactically. Humanized versions of JUNV-1A2, JUNV-1D5, and JUNV-5B12 mAbs, which showed protection in vivo in the Stat2 −/− surrogate model, were produced. These antibodies were evaluated in a guinea pig challenge model of AHF and showed protective efficacy. Escape experiments with these humanized antibodies, as well as previously characterized antibodies, GB03 and JUN1, using rVSV-JUNV resulted in the acquisition of amino acid changes in the GP1 part of the GPC, which directly contacts host receptor transferrin receptor 1, indicating these sites could be key for future therapies. In summary, we generated mAbs that may be valuable for antibody-guided vaccine design and therapeutic development. IMPORTANCE Junín virus (JUNV) is a highly pathogenic virus that causes Argentine hemorrhagic fever (AHF) and is classified as a category A pathogen due to its potential for aerosol transmission and the significant number of annual infections and deaths associated with it. Although effective treatments exist, such as convalescent immune plasma, their availability is limited, and they are ineffective when given after the first week of symptoms. This study is significant because it focuses on developing therapeutic monoclonal antibodies against JUNV with strong in vitro neutralizing activity and protection in both a surrogate mouse model and a guinea pig challenge model of AHF. This has led to promising antibody candidates that could be used as therapeutics to combat ongoing outbreaks.

title: Predicted spatial distribution of the primary Lassa virus reservoir, the multimammate mouse, in Africa
abstract: Objective This study predicts the potential spatial distribution of the multimammate mouse ( Mastomys natalensis ), the primary host of Lassa virus, a major public health concern across West Africa. Methods Correlative maximum entropy models were constructed with occurrence records of M. natalensis from Global Biodiversity Information Facility, using long-term bioclimatic variables at ~1 km resolution as predictors. Candidate models were evaluated and best models were selected based on statistical significance, predictive ability, and model fitting and complexity. Models were projected to the African continent. Results Median predictions from the best-supported models indicated extensive areas of moderate to high suitability across sub-Saharan Africa, with suitability concentrated within the tropical and subtropical belts of West, Central, and East Africa. Suitability declined sharply across arid regions, particularly the Sahara and parts of the Horn of Africa. Within Nigeria, a focal area of the study, the predicted suitability was broadly high across southern and central regions, with a gradual decline toward Sahel-adjacent northern areas. Sub-national projections for Lagos, Oyo, Edo, Kano, and the Federal Capital Territory revealed spatial heterogeneity in suitability, consistent with underlying climatic gradients in temperature and precipitation that shape habitat conditions for M. Conclusion These findings provide a spatial framework for prioritizing rodent surveillance and supporting targeted Lassa fever preparedness and control strategies.
